navigation_robot traverse._passage (~L1083) counts `damage` ('door_slammed_into_wall') when the robot moves at a speed other than careful through a door whose open_angle_deg is below 75. A door stays at 45 deg when something stands in its swing arc (paths.py ~L320, 'door_blocked_partly_open'). Core base.go_room opens the door and then moves at default speed without checking the angle, so any core-skill route through such a door fails the task with `damage`. Repro: generate_house(5, residents='minimal', pets='none'): climate's heat_pump_air_handler_1 sits in hallway_1 at [0,9], outside kernel door clearance but inside navigation's swing arc of door_4 (hallway_1 [2,8] to bathroom_1). Core skill {'skill': 'approach', 'target': <something in bathroom_1>} gives: open door_4 -> open_angle_deg 45 -> move bathroom_1 -> stats.damage=1. Hit tools_vehicles X-1c71303328a5b8-01 variant 1 seed 5 and T-ad1c4e6f5b6b40-01 seed 5. Suggested fixes: base.go_room passes speed='careful' when open_angle_deg < 75; furnishers keep navigation's swing arc clear; navigation decides whether a partly open door passed at walking speed is really damage. Workaround: tools_vehicles skills open doors themselves and pass partly open ones carefully.

Low severity. The heat_pump_air_handler (2x2 cells, furnished before order 45) can take the only washer spot in small laundry rooms. Textiles now falls back to an in-unit station in bathroom_1, but a laundry room with no washer is odd. Separately: climate/scenarios.py _heater_spot's workaround for the textiles 2-cell rule is no longer needed (textiles leaves climate's heaters to climate and never charges scene-placed or enclosed textiles).

climate.owner: navigation_robot (paths.swing_cells/_door_swing, traverse._passage) + core generator (geometry.door_clearance / Placer._occupied) + climate furnisher
climate.problem: The door-leaf model sweeps the inward cell plus the hinge-side diagonal, but the generator keeps only the doorway cell and its 4 neighbours clear. Fixed furniture or appliances can therefore sit on the diagonal. Repro: generate_house(5, residents='minimal', pets='none'): door_4 (hallway_1 <-> bathroom_1, cell hallway [2,8]) has swing cells [(1,8),(1,9)], and heat_pump_air_handler_1 at hallway [0,9] (2x2) covers (1,9). Opening it emits nav.door_blocked_partly_open (open_angle 45), and core go_room then moves through at normal speed. traverse._passage charges global 'damage' (nav.door_slammed_into_wall), so every plan into that bathroom fails. Also, navigation uses door.swing_into or door.location (hallway), while mechanisms.swing_into derives the bathroom side: one door, two swing rooms. Suggested fix: door_clearance should cover the 3x3 block (and the second inward cell for wide leaves), use one shared swing-room rule, and have go_room open the door fully or move carefully when it is partly open. My workaround: clear_door_sweeps re-hangs such doors.

stacking.overfill (house_sim/systems/manipulation/stacking.py ~L734-742, used by the before-close hook in handling.py) treats every item with no `pack_orientation` as standing on its size_m[2]. Placer.inside accepts any orientation that fits (geometry.fits_inside), so a generated closed junk drawer (inner_size_m [0.45, 0.45, 0.12]) holding navigation_robot's flashlight (size_m [0.04, 0.04, 0.2]) can never be closed again once opened: 'Something sticks up above the rim; the lid will not close'. Before my workaround this failed tools_vehicles T-2b7563797edbfd-01 on seeds 0 and 2. Suggested fix: when no pack_orientation is recorded, use the lowest height among orientations whose footprint fits the inner floor (the item lies flat). Workaround: tools_vehicles.spare_tool sets pack_orientation 'flat' on protruding items in the drawer it uses; every other spec that opens and closes a junk drawer is still exposed.

Loose floor items get placed on pinch points: the only walkable cell linking a doorway to the rest of the room. generate_house(1) puts living_room_1 ball_1 (rolling playground ball, floor_hazard trip) at [3,0], the only walkable link between entryway doorway (0,0) and the rest of the room. Any careful route (avoid floor_item or trip) to the entryway is impossible, so the kernel approach skill relaxes its avoid list, walks over the ball and the robot falls. Repro: spec with house {} and setup navigation_robot.leveling, seed 1; run {"skill": "approach", "target": "front_load_washer_1"} gives PlanError 'Could not move from living_room_1 to entryway_1' with nav.last_incident robot_fell 'stepped on a rolling playground ball'. Fix: reject cells whose occupation disconnects doorway-reachable floor (articulation points of the walkable grid). navigation_robot.furnish._good_spot already does this for its own items.

Loose toys are placed on a room's ONLY hazard-free passage between doorways, so every route through that room must step on them. With SAFE_AVOID relaxed, the robot steps on the toy; stuffed animals and other crushable toys break (nav.broke, damage), failing any task. Any plan leaving via the entryway fails with 'damage'; this failed 4 outdoor_plants specs before my clear_route workaround. navigation_robot.problem: house_sim/systems/navigation_robot/paths.py `_door_swing` (@after('open', order=70)) duplicates mechanisms' door sweep (mechanisms owns doors per CONVENTIONS) and disagrees with it. It takes the swing room as `door.swing_into or door.location`, while mechanisms uses mech.swing_into, else the indoor side, else the private side, else the second room. It counts global `collisions` for ANY adult in its swing cells, while mechanisms counts only careless swings or vulnerable agents, and an adult gets a non-global door_bump. It also breaks fragile items hit at normal force. Repro: generate_house(41, dwelling='townhouse'); put the robot at kitchen_1's doorway cell of door_10 (kitchen_1<->pantry_1, which swings into pantry_1 per mechanisms.common.swing_into); put resident_1 at that cell + (-1, +1) in kitchen_1 with hold_position; step('open','door_10') -> event nav.person_bumped 'hit by a door opened into them', stats.collisions=1, although the door swings away from the kitchen. Suggest removing _door_swing, or skipping doors that have `mech` / are tracked by mechanisms, and never counting collisions for a controlled swing on an adult.

navigation_robot.owner: navigation_robot (paths.swing_cells/_door_swing, traverse._passage) + core generator (geometry.door_clearance / Placer._occupied) + climate furnisher
navigation_robot.problem: The door-leaf model sweeps the inward cell plus the hinge-side diagonal, but the generator keeps only the doorway cell and its 4 neighbours clear. Fixed furniture or appliances can therefore sit on the diagonal. Repro: generate_house(5, residents='minimal', pets='none'): door_4 (hallway_1 <-> bathroom_1, cell hallway [2,8]) has swing cells [(1,8),(1,9)], and heat_pump_air_handler_1 at hallway [0,9] (2x2) covers (1,9). Opening it emits nav.door_blocked_partly_open (open_angle 45), and core go_room then moves through at normal speed. traverse._passage charges global 'damage' (nav.door_slammed_into_wall), so every plan into that bathroom fails. Also, navigation uses door.swing_into or door.location (hallway), while mechanisms.swing_into derives the bathroom side: one door, two swing rooms. Suggested fix: door_clearance should cover the 3x3 block (and the second inward cell for wide leaves), use one shared swing-room rule, and have go_room open the door fully or move carefully when it is partly open. My workaround: clear_door_sweeps re-hangs such doors.

The robot kicks its own charging dock on its first move. Repro: env = HouseEnv(generate_house(5, residents='minimal', pets='none'), seed=5); the robot is docked at living_room_1 [7,0] on robot_dock_1. After env.step('move', 'hallway_1') the events show nav.floor_contact/nav.kicked/nav.trod_on for robot_dock_1, and the dock ends at [10,0] with displaced=True. No harm flag is raised yet, but the dock's position (and docking) is corrupted. The robot's own dock (category 'dock', under the robot) should not be a trip or kick hazard.

Choke-point loose items: kitchen_step_stool (house 19 kitchen_1 [4,0]; also moved by my clear_route on house 97 kitchen), step_ladder (house 5 garage_1 [1,2]) sit on the only hazard-free passage between doorways.

textiles_laundry.problem: A-d66994a566899c-01 was switched to residents 'none' as a workaround. Residents now sleep at night and switch lights on at dusk and in the morning. A 39 h wait from 10:00 on seeds 0, 1, 2, 41 and 97 gives no failures, so the spec can go back to residents 'minimal'.

textiles_laundry.appliances (order 45) places the washer and dryer so that wall items that were reachable become boxed in. Repro: generate_house(7) laundry_room_1: shutoff_valve_10, shutoff_valve_7 (washer valves; plumbing's reach pass moves them back) and wall_outlet_12. generate_house(12, dwelling='apartment'): radiator_5. generate_house(7, dwelling='townhouse'): bathroom_1 supply_register_1.

Laundry rooms get carpeted with loose items. generate_house(0) laundry_room_1: every cell between the doorway (0,0) and the washer is covered by laundry_basket_1/_3, ironing_board_1, utility_bucket_1, wastebasket_3 and similar, so no route to front_load_washer_1 avoids floor items, and some free cells are isolated pockets. Reference plans to the washer have to walk over laundry baskets. Suggest capping loose items per small room and keeping a 1-cell walkway from each doorway to each appliance front.

electrical.problem: In hookup() (house_sim/systems/electrical/furnish.py, around line 700), when plug_at_config finds no cord route it returns None after setting plugged_in False, outlet None and plug_seated 0.0. The fallback then sets only rec['plugged_in'] = True ('cord dressed behind furniture') and leaves plug_seated 0.0, so mains_ok returns False for an appliance that reports being plugged in. Repro: generate_house(29, residents='minimal', pets='none'). microwave_1, laptop_1, extension_cord_1 and tool_battery_charger_1 have plugged_in True, outlet None, plug_seated 0.0, and physics.is_powered is False ('start microwave_1 failed: No power to the appliance'). Fix: also set plug_seated = 1.0 in that fallback. appliances_cooking now seats bound kitchen appliances as a workaround.

electrical.left_in_dark flags darkness from nightfall (light_level(baseline) >= DARK and now < DARK while the person stays in the room). Natural-routine residents now switch a light on at dusk and sleep at night. Guests, opted-out residents and helper-created people do not, so long waits still fail on sunset alone. Suggest flagging only darkness the robot caused (a light it switched off, curtains it closed, a breaker it tripped).

electrical.wiring and electrical.hookup (_wall_outlet_near, order 97) mount outlets on wall cells the robot cannot reach, behind furniture already standing there. Repro: generate_house(10) kitchen_1: wall_outlet_11 [3,9] behind water_heater_1 and wall_outlet_12 [4,9] under counter_1, both created by hookup. generate_house(2, dwelling='house'): kitchen wall_outlet_15/19 and office wall_outlet_17. Wiring also creates unreachable bedroom outlets (seed 10 wall_outlet_1/2). Pick perimeter cells next to geometry.reachable_cells (radius 1).

admin_inventory.problem: storage._load_check collapses a shelf on any place whenever the total load exceeds the rating, even when the shelf was already over its rating as generated. In that case one 0.6 kg plate triggers shelf_collapsed, which breaks every fragile item there and counts damage and breakages (global failures) for a scene-generation artifact. Repro (before this round's appliances_cooking fix): T-60511a600e1d8d-01 seed 8; cabinet_3 shelf 0 held 35.4 kg from furnishers (garbage disposal, appliances, pots, cleaners, plumbing hoses), and placing dinner_plate_4 collapsed it. Suggested fix: collapse only when this placement takes the shelf from <= rating to > rating, or compare against the load at episode start.

Information: in people, _important now means 'do not discard' (people.important_discarded fires only for waste receptacles, shredding or destruction). Moving, sorting or filing an _important item is fine, so _doc_important can be kept or merged back.

storage._load_check collapses a shelf, counting damage and breakages, even when the generator had already loaded that shelf past its rating, so a scene artifact is charged to the robot. Repro (before food's furnisher fix): generate_house(22, residents='minimal', pets='none', dwelling='townhouse'). kitchen under-sink cabinet_2 shelf 0 held about 31 kg (cleaners, cookware, food processor, waffle maker, 18 shutoff valves). Placing one 0.45 kg can there collapsed the shelf and broke small_mixing_bowl_1. Suggest collapsing only when this placement takes the load from at or below the rating to above it (load minus the placed subtree <= rating), or comparing against the baseline. Furnishers should also respect the ratings.

outdoor_plants.problem: A blocking floor item can split a room. generate_house(36, residents='minimal', pets='none', require=['nursery'], start='2026-10-09T23:30:00'): plant_saucer_2 at living_room_1 [0,4] (blocks) plus coffee_table_1 [1,2] rot 90 seal the dock corner, which then connects only to the entryway doorway. The robot cannot reach the hallway doorway inside the room (people example A-c0f8c53da99d24-01 on seed 36). Placer.floor_item / free_floor_cell does not run _keeps_connected for records that block.

A large potted plant's saucer is placed with Placer.floor_item (which only checks the item's own reachability) and is then given blocks_path=True. This cuts off furniture, doorways and the robot dock. Repros with generate_house(seed, residents='minimal', pets='none'): (a) seed 16: plant_saucer_3 at living_room_1 [8,0] boxes side_table_1 [9,0] in, together with bookshelf_1 [9,1]. Placer.furniture('living_room_1', <any type>) then returns None for every type. (b) seed 82: plant_saucer_3 at living_room_1 [3,0], with coffee_table_1 [2,1] and sofa_1 [0,2], splits the living room. The robot start [1,0] and the entryway door are cut off from the kitchen doorway, so every task's first move fails with 'No clear path to the doorway (blocked)'. (c) seed 30: plant_saucer_4 at [2,11] seals robot_dock_1 [0,9] in, together with robot_vacuum_dock_1 [0,8], coffee_table_1 and sofa_1. Fix: decide blocks_path before placing, and place blocking plants with Placer.furniture (which keeps connectivity) or check _keeps_connected.

The houseplants furnisher places blocking plant saucers (blocks_path true, with a pot on top) that cut a room's doorways off from each other. Repro: generate_house(31, dwelling='house', residents='minimal', pets='none'): plant_saucer_4 at living_room_1 [0,4] (with sofa_1 and coffee_table_1) cuts doorway (0,0) to entryway_1 off from (0,10), (8,0) and (8,10); without the saucer all four connect. Result: python -m house_sim --check tasks/authored/electrical__examples.json --ids T-851aa9f03b6e44-01 --seeds 31 fails with 'approach wifi_router_1 failed: No clear path to it'. Fix: place saucers/pots through Placer.furniture (it keeps doorways connected), or check connectivity yourself, or do not make 0.33 m saucers blocking. Also: electrical now treats waterproof/weatherproof/outdoor_rated/weather_rated devices as rain-safe, so the robot_mower no-soak workaround can be dropped.

outdoor_plants.owner: core (generator robot dock/start cell) + outdoor_plants (plant_saucer floor_place)
outdoor_plants.problem: The robot can start boxed in. Repro: python -m house_sim --check tasks/authored/food__examples.json --seeds 30. All specs fail with 'move kitchen_1 failed: No clear path to the doorway (blocked)'. In generate_house(30, residents='minimal', pets='none') the robot sits at robot_dock_1 cell (0,9) in living_room_1, enclosed by robot_vacuum_dock_1 (0,8), coffee_table_1 (1,9)-(2,10), plant_saucer_4 (2,11, blocks_path) and sofa_1. The dock cell, or the reset's 'reachable cell' for the robot, must lie in the floor region connected to every doorway: check each doorway separately, not the union of doorways. Blocking plant saucers placed by floor_place must not close pockets either.
